provenance_note: script_sha256 identifies this rebuild/evaluation script. Indexed solves and checks retain their original executed probe source in the recorded code snapshots.

conventions.comparison: Fixed nominal 0-1 Rabi-rate bound: amplitude 0.06/|n01|, du and ddu 0.1/|n01|, in authored units. Alternate: unchanged first-gate raw bounds.
conventions.best: Highest replay fidelity among the three primary GRAPE seeds passing constraints; failures retained.
conventions.evaluation: Returned amplitudes and knots; nominal carriers, phases, frame and bounds fixed. Perturbed charge operator at authored scale. Closed RWA model only.
conventions.logical_states: Each perturbed model's eigenstates, with overlapping charge-basis eigenvectors matched in sign. Quasistatic variation, preparation in actual levels.
conventions.resolution: Sampled refinement sensitivity only: nominal separation exceeds 1e-7 and the sum of nominal refinement changes. This says nothing about optimizer resolution; solver variability prevents a nominal device ranking. 1e-7 is an agreement floor, not an error bound; uncertainty rankings also remain unresolved.
conventions.sampling: Five charge samples, two one-at-a-time EJ samples and the combined individually worst pair; worst sampled, not worst case over a region.
conventions.EJ_sampling_reason: A common +/-0.1% EJ perturbation gives approximately 2.9-5.5 MHz detunings across the selected devices, a visible fixed-pulse stress over 20 ns while remaining a small fractional parameter change. This is a declared probe assumption, not a fabrication distribution.
conventions.refinement: Four replays per candidate: nominal/original worst point, levels 3->5 and cutoff 30->40 separately. No inference about which refined sample is worst.
conventions.timings: CPU workstation, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1. Runner job wall time excludes launch checks; launch elapsed includes them. First objective call includes compilation; evaluations include model/sign construction. Dynamiqs open-system time includes cold compilation.

candidate_choice: 10, 30, 60 fF span sampled dispersion of about 58 MHz, 0.75 MHz and 5.6 kHz; smaller Csh increases anharmonicity while increasing charge sensitivity. 60 fF retains the first gate. Actual gate sensitivity is measured below, not inferred from dispersion alone.

open_system.operator: A=sum(sqrt(k)|k-1><k|), collapse=sqrt(gamma)*A tensor I_ancilla; gamma=1e-5/ns (assumed 100 us T1)
open_system.scope: Feasibility/cost within the declared RWA model; assumed common relaxation rate, no design-dependent relaxation claim. Authored data, no new check.

reading.transition: entanglix.corrector.metrics.spectral_arrays(system, 2, {}) returns energies; f01 is their difference. There is no dedicated named-transition resolver.
reading.per_candidate_inputs: Copy system.toml and change Csh; compute f01; set the same nominal frame and both carriers; set amplitude/du/ddu bounds under the declared policy. Evaluation retains those values.
reading.perturbed_inputs: EJ is a named parameter, but control has no parameter override. Offset charge is literal model data. Both currently need a separate system file and adjacent control spec; evaluations here are probe code.
reading.sweep_point: A copied adjacent sweep-point system.toml can be control.system. CLI/Python parent_run_ids can name the sweep run, but no field binds its point index. MCP control exposes no parent_run_ids. A referenced file inside spec/points cannot be named directly because control.system must be beside the control input.
reading.decisions: Three known exact control bases can share one revision and one start decision, provided all job/check operations are allowed. A fourth adaptive candidate requires one approve-revision decision. Checkpoint assessments are findings, not user decisions; optional reviews or limits can add decisions only if declared.
reading.authored_evaluation: An exact run-script base can hold the evaluation script, system.toml, pulse.npz and numerical data beside the system. Each candidate/perturbation-dependent bundle needs its own approved base. Its authored fidelity metrics and evidence stay authored data, not built-in check outcomes.
reading.variation_binding: Control variation would need to bind system parameter overrides, nominal transition selection, frame/carrier derivation and the chosen amplitude/derivative-bound policy. Current admission accepts exact control bundles only.

c30_raw_pulse_under_rabi_bounds.evidence: In-process constraints evaluation of the retained raw-bound pulse against the retained Rabi-rate input; no solve or verification job added.

optimizer_interpretation.followup_scope: The named matched-seed solves would test whether the attained fidelities stabilize under the primary policy; a finite seed set cannot certify a global optimum. The retained admissible raw-bound pulse already disproves a device-limited explanation for the 30 fF primary deficit.

answers.1: At Csh=10/30/60 fF, sampled charge dispersions are 57.5912/0.749746/0.00560865 MHz and anharmonicities are -1.44029/-0.59236/-0.317214 GHz. The selected set spans charge sensitivity and leakage-related level spacing while retaining the first-gate device.
answers.2: Frame and carriers shifted together by 1 MHz are accepted; carriers shifted alone are refused by channel name. See the retained detuning entries for exact outcomes.
answers.3: The 12 retained solves include a 30 fF raw-bound pulse with replay fidelity 0.9999999996 that also passes the Rabi-rate constraints, versus the primary best 0.9897697808; the primary results are suboptimal local solutions. Solver variability prevents interpreting nominal candidate differences: seed spreads at 10/30/60 fF are 0.022947/0.000168441/0.000384956, versus the 10-to-60 fF separation 2.6e-09; the additional matched-seed solves are named but were not run.
answers.4: Worst sampled fidelities at 10/30/60 fF are 0.436341682/0.972246977/0.991176814; the 30 fF values come from the selected local-optimum pulse, not the higher-fidelity admissible raw-bound pulse. All uncertainty rankings remain unresolved because only each original worst point was refined, and the samples do not establish a continuous-region worst case.
answers.5: Levels 3->5 change nominal fidelity by 6.26e-09/0.000288/1.66e-05 and original-worst-point fidelity by 5.12e-07/0.000965/9.23e-05 at 10/30/60 fF; cutoff 30->40 changes fidelity by at most 5.8e-12. Four replays per candidate cover only those selected points and do not establish convergence of the sampled minimum.
answers.6: With the assumed 1e-5/ns relaxation rate, the passive-ancilla evaluations agree between CPU engines within 3.94e-13 in fidelity. This is feasibility evidence for an assumed channel, not design-dependent relaxation.
answers.7: Existing operations compose with exact bases. Particular sweep-point binding, MCP parent lineage and parameter-dependent control data are the recorded gaps; authored evaluation is another exact script bundle.
answers.8: The original item 3-5 full-pass elapsed time is 214.284 s; retained solver job time totals 193.541 s and check job time 8.724 s. This invocation took 1.385 s for items 3-5, including 1.157 s of direct evaluations; indexed-job reuse is True.
